headline: Medium risk: shared content and broad egress create leakage and injection pathways; no direct evidence of a dangerous default interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and issue/task content, while Rasa consumes external messages from chat channels. If Plane output is copied into Rasa training or responses, attacker-controlled text could steer behavior. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred from documented surfaces rather than observed interaction.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads are forwarded into Rasa prompts, rules, or training data
IF a shared workspace or chat bridge is added between Plane and Rasa
mitigations: Disable any automatic copy from Plane exports into Rasa inputs
Add a manual review step before importing Plane content into Rasa
Strip instructions and markup from uploaded files before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to content passed between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, images, hyperlinks, notes, and has broad network egress; Rasa handles text and voice and can send messages through third-party channels. If the same sensitive ticket or attachment is routed through both, leakage can occur through outbound integrations. No shared filesystem is documented, so the risk is inferred but plausible.
conditions: IF sensitive Plane attachments are forwarded into Rasa channels
IF Rasa is connected to external messaging APIs carrying Plane content
mitigations: Restrict which Plane fields may be exported to Rasa
Redact attachments before sending them to chat channels
Review outbound API destinations in Rasa
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane does not write the filesystem, while Rasa does not advertise filesystem write or shared mutable resource access here. Their documented capabilities overlap mainly on network egress and external APIs, which is not enough for a write-write conflict. Uncertainty is low because no shared write surface is shown.
conditions: IF an operator adds a shared writable directory or database to both systems
IF both are granted the same mutable OAuth-scoped resource
mitigations: Keep Plane and Rasa on separate storage backends
Avoid granting both agents the same write credentials
Use per-agent service accounts for integrations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane produces issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, and notes that Rasa could ingest as conversational context or support content. If Rasa treats that output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect replies or actions. The pair has no built-in verification link documented, so the pathway is inferred and should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF Rasa uses Plane-generated tickets as source-of-truth answers
IF Plane summaries are inserted into Rasa without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before Rasa uses Plane content
Mark Plane-derived text as untrusted in Rasa prompts
Add a verification checklist for support replies
requires-engineering: add source attribution and confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: Plane is self-hostable and open-source, while Rasa is also open-source with allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to operator configuration rather than the pair itself. I do not cite only one agent because the issue is the absence of a mismatch across both profiles.
conditions: IF the operator routes regulated data through a non-compliant external API
IF retention settings differ between Plane exports and Rasa channel logs
mitigations: Review retention settings on both systems
Keep regulated data out of external messaging channels
Document the data flow for each integration
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across deployments
